   "source": [
    "# Fourier-domain single-pulsar analysis: marginalizing DM in step 1\n",
    "\n",
    "This tutorial runs the two-step Fourier-domain likelihood of Valtolina & van Haasteren (2025, \"VvH25\"), with the\n",
    "Gaussian-mixture (GMM) generalization, on a single pulsar, and checks it against an ordinary time-domain analysis.\n",
    "\n",
    "**The question.** In step 1 we summarize what one pulsar's data say about its *achromatic* red-noise Fourier\n",
    "coefficients $\\mathbf a$, with everything else -- timing model, white noise, and here a dispersion-measure (DM)\n",
    "Gaussian process with free hyperparameters -- marginalized. In step 2 we infer the red-noise spectrum $\\boldsymbol\\eta$\n",
    "(here a power law, $\\log_{10}A, \\gamma$) from that summary alone. If the summary is good, the step-2 posterior on\n",
    "$\\boldsymbol\\eta$ matches the time-domain posterior, which samples DM and red noise together.\n",
    "\n",
    "VvH25 summarize with a single Gaussian $\\mathcal N(\\mathbf a\\mid\\hat{\\mathbf a}_0,\\boldsymbol\\Sigma_0)$. When the\n",
    "marginalized parameters (the DM hyperparameters $\\boldsymbol\\theta$) are covariant with the red noise, the true marginal\n",
    "$\\int d\\boldsymbol\\theta\\, p(\\boldsymbol\\theta\\mid\\delta t)\\,\\mathcal N(\\mathbf a\\mid\\hat{\\mathbf a}(\\boldsymbol\\theta),\\boldsymbol\\Sigma(\\boldsymbol\\theta))$\n",
    "is a *mixture* of Gaussians, and the single Gaussian can fail. J1738+0333 in EPTA DR2 is such a case: it is observed\n",
    "at nearly one radio frequency, so DM and achromatic noise are hard to tell apart.\n",
    "\n",
    "We compare three estimates of the red-noise posterior:\n",
    "\n",
    "| | model | coefficients |\n",
    "|---|---|---|\n",
    "| **A** | time domain, DM + red noise sampled together (the reference) | marginalized |\n",
    "| **B** | Fourier domain, Gaussian summary (VvH25) | marginalized |\n",
    "| **C** | Fourier domain, GMM summary as a correction term | sampled, decentered |\n",
    "\n",
    "C is the template for any non-Gaussian summary density -- a GMM, a normalizing flow, a heavy-tailed\n",
    "distribution, ... The GMM can also be marginalized analytically; that route is shown at the end, evaluated at a few\n",
    "points rather than sampled, because its cost grows with the number of mixture components."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "4ba90e5e",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-07T16:24:51.217613Z",

   "source": [
    "## The pulsar and the models\n",
    "\n",
    "Noise settings follow the EPTA DR2 analyses this example was first developed on: 30 achromatic red-noise and 30 DM\n",
    "frequencies over the pulsar's span, and white noise fixed to the EPTA noise dictionary. The step-1 reference spectrum\n",
    "$\\boldsymbol\\eta_0$ is deliberately loud ($\\log_{10}A_0=-11.1$): step 2 divides out the reference prior\n",
    "$\\mathcal N(\\mathbf a\\mid 0,\\boldsymbol\\varphi_0)$, which must not constrain the coefficients more than the data do\n",
    "(see VvH25, App. A)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "a8504020",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-07T16:24:52.621974Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-07T16:24:52.621831Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-07T16:24:52.628816Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-07T16:24:52.628601Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "datapath = Path(ds.__path__[0]) / '../../data/epta_dr2'\n",
    "psr = ds.Pulsar.read_feather(datapath / 'J1738+0333.feather')\n",
    "\n",
    "T = ds.getspan(psr)\n",
    "NRN, NDM = 30, 30\n",
    "\n",
    "eta0 = {f'{psr.name}_red_noise_log10_A': -11.1,      # step-1 reference spectrum\n",
    "        f'{psr.name}_red_noise_gamma': 3.0}\n",
    "\n",
    "# update if need chromgp, for example\n",
    "priordict = {'(.*_)?dm_gp_log10_A': [-20, -11], '(.*_)?dm_gp_gamma': [0, 7],\n",
    "             '(.*_)?red_noise_log10_A': [-20, -11], '(.*_)?red_noise_gamma': [0, 7]}\n",
    "\n",
    "def run_nuts(logl, num_warmup=500, num_samples=2000, seed=0):\n",
    "    # discovery will also make numpyro models for you if you want\n",
    "    model = ds_numpyro.makemodel_transformed(logl, priordict=priordict)\n",
    "    sampler = ds_numpyro.makesampler_nuts(model, num_warmup=num_warmup, num_samples=num_samples)\n",
    "    t = time.time()\n",
    "    sampler.run(jax.random.key(seed))\n",
    "    print(f'{time.time() - t:.0f} s')\n",
    "    return sampler.to_df()\n",
    "\n",
    "rn_pars = [f'{psr.name}_red_noise_log10_A', f'{psr.name}_red_noise_gamma']"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0e23586a",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The time-domain likelihood with both GPs. It serves twice: sampled with everything free it is the reference\n",
    "**A**; with the red-noise spectrum held at $\\boldsymbol\\eta_0$ it is the step-1 likelihood."
   ]
  },

   ]

   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Step 1: summarize the red-noise coefficients\n",
    "\n",
    "Hold the red noise at $\\boldsymbol\\eta_0$ and sample the DM hyperparameters $\\boldsymbol\\theta$ from\n",
    "$p(\\boldsymbol\\theta\\mid\\delta t,\\boldsymbol\\eta_0)$, with all Fourier coefficients marginalized analytically.\n",
    "Any sampler would do; this is just `logL` with two parameters fixed."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "f7d0909a",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-07T16:25:25.444778Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-07T16:25:25.444680Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-07T16:25:30.621365Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-07T16:25:30.621072Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "5 s\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# hack it so that we fix the likelihood\n",
    "# so always add eta0.\n",
    "def logL_step1(params):\n",
    "    return psl.logL({**params, **eta0})\n",
    "# if you have chromgp then you'll need \"or chromgp in par\" for example\n",
    "# or you can just *exclude* intrinsic red noise parameters.\n",
    "# the point is just that we fix red noise to the parameters\n",
    "# in eta0\n",
    "logL_step1.params = [par for par in psl.logL.params if 'dm_gp' in par]\n",
    "\n",
    "chain1 = run_nuts(jax.jit(logL_step1))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "411a0fd0",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "For each sample $\\boldsymbol\\theta_k$, the red-noise coefficients are Gaussian,\n",
    "$\\mathcal N(\\mathbf a\\mid\\hat{\\mathbf a}(\\boldsymbol\\theta_k),\\boldsymbol\\Sigma(\\boldsymbol\\theta_k))$ (the pulsar\n",
    "likelihood's `conditional`, with the DM coefficients integrated out). `summarize_pulsar` evaluates these and combines\n",
    "them by the law of total expectation and covariance (draft Eq. 14):\n",
    "\n",
    "$$\\hat{\\mathbf a}_0 = \\mathbb E_k[\\hat{\\mathbf a}(\\boldsymbol\\theta_k)],\\qquad\n",
    "\\boldsymbol\\Sigma_0 = \\mathbb E_k[\\boldsymbol\\Sigma(\\boldsymbol\\theta_k)] + \\mathrm{Cov}_k[\\hat{\\mathbf a}(\\boldsymbol\\theta_k)].$$\n",
    "\n",
    "It keeps the per-sample pairs too: they are the mixture components below. Passing arrays for some parameters is\n",
    "what tells it to average; passing only scalars gives the summary at fixed noise."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "f83b2fb7",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-07T16:25:30.622581Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-07T16:25:30.622508Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-07T16:25:31.268049Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-07T16:25:31.267768Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "((60,), (2000, 60))"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 6,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "samples = {par: chain1[par].values for par in logL_step1.params}\n",
    "\n",
    "# summarize_pulsar contains all of the info we'd need to run\n",
    "# the Valtolina/van Haasteren method, or the new GMM method.\n",
    "summary = fpta.summarize_pulsar(psr, psl, {**samples, **eta0})\n",
    "\n",
    "summary.ahat0.shape, summary.ahat_samples.shape"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "abd428df",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Step 2\n",
    "\n",
    "A `FourierSummary` doubles as a *stand-in pulsar*: as a function of $\\mathbf a$, the summary with the reference prior\n",
    "divided out,\n",
    "$\\log\\mathcal N(\\mathbf a\\mid\\hat{\\mathbf a}_0,\\boldsymbol\\Sigma_0) - \\log\\mathcal N(\\mathbf a\\mid 0,\\boldsymbol\\varphi_0)$,\n",
    "has exactly the form of a pulsar likelihood $\\log p(\\delta t\\mid\\mathbf a)$ with\n",
    "\n",
    "$$F^\\top N^{-1}F \\;\\to\\; \\boldsymbol\\Sigma_0^{-1}-\\boldsymbol\\varphi_0^{-1},\\qquad F^\\top N^{-1}\\delta t \\;\\to\\; \\boldsymbol\\Sigma_0^{-1}\\hat{\\mathbf a}_0 .$$\n",
    "\n",
    "So step 2 uses the ordinary discovery GP and likelihood constructors; the only changes are the stand-in's data\n",
    "(`summary.residuals`, unit white noise from `makenoise_summary`) and `fourierbasis=fpta.summarybasis` on its GPs.\n",
    "(The same works for whole arrays, with `makecommongp_fourier` / `makeglobalgp_fourier` -- including HD.)\n",
    "\n",
    "### B. Gaussian summary (VvH25)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "1bbbd763",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-07T16:25:31.269240Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-07T16:25:31.269168Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-07T16:25:35.569810Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-07T16:25:35.569559Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "4 s\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "rn = ds.makegp_fourier(summary, ds.powerlaw, NRN, T=T, fourierbasis=fpta.summarybasis, name='red_noise')\n",
    "pslB = ds.PulsarLikelihood([summary.residuals, fpta.makenoise_summary(summary), rn])\n",
    "\n",
    "chainB = run_nuts(jax.jit(pslB.logL))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f8a0dd18",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### C. GMM summary as a correction, coefficients sampled\n",
    "\n",
    "The general route, for any non-Gaussian summary density. Write the density $q$ in whitened coordinates\n",
    "$\\mathbf y = \\mathbf L_0^{-1}(\\mathbf a-\\hat{\\mathbf a}_0)$, $\\mathbf L_0 = \\mathrm{chol}(\\boldsymbol\\Sigma_0)$, where the\n",
    "Gaussian summary is $\\mathcal N(\\mathbf y\\mid 0,\\mathbf I)$. Step 2 then gains a per-pulsar correction (draft Eq. 28, 34)\n",
    "\n",
    "$$\\log w(\\mathbf a) = \\log q(\\mathbf y) - \\log\\mathcal N(\\mathbf y\\mid 0,\\mathbf I)$$\n",
    "\n",
    "on top of the Gaussian-summary likelihood. It cannot be integrated out, so the coefficients are sampled, with the\n",
    "CURN-style decentering of `ArrayLikelihood(..., decenter=True)` to avoid Neal's funnel.\n",
    "\n",
    "The density goes on the summary (`summary.density`, anything with a `log_prob(y)` method: `summary.mixture(K)`, or a\n",
    "trained `flowjax` flow), and `makecorrection(summary)` turns it into a term of the stand-in's `PulsarLikelihood`. The\n",
    "pulsar's `clogL`, and the `clogL` of any `ArrayLikelihood` containing it, add the term at the sampled coefficients.\n",
    "\n",
    "The mixture is that of the step-1 conditionals (draft Eq. 19, A8),\n",
    "$q(\\mathbf a) = \\frac1K\\sum_k\\mathcal N(\\mathbf a\\mid\\hat{\\mathbf a}(\\boldsymbol\\theta_k),\\boldsymbol\\Sigma(\\boldsymbol\\theta_k))$,\n",
    "with $K$ samples spaced evenly through the step-1 chain. **$K$ matters**: the non-Gaussian tails are carried by a few\n",
    "rare components, and for this pulsar $K=64$ still gives (wrongly) the Gaussian answer while $K=512$ matches the time\n",
    "domain. The prior swap is importance sampling from the reference spectrum $\\boldsymbol\\varphi_0$ to $\\boldsymbol\\varphi(\\boldsymbol\\eta)$,\n",
    "so a loud $\\boldsymbol\\eta_0$ is always valid but needs more components."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "id": "4243e6c4",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-07T16:25:35.570985Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-07T16:25:35.570896Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-07T16:25:35.797325Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-07T16:25:35.797048Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "K = 512\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "K_reduced = 16\n",
    "# improved approximation to the marginal\n",
    "# in this case a gaussian mixture with K components\n",
    "# summary was made with however many samples was passed to it,\n",
    "# so K just needs to be less than the number of samples\n",
    "summary.density = summary.mixture(K)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Above is an equal weighted mixture. We can reduce the overall size of the mixture\n",
    "# by combining Gaussians and weighting them unequally. Mentioned in the draft, but not shown\n",
    "# uses: Runnalls 2007, IEEE Trans. Aerosp. Electron. Syst. 43, 989;\n",
    "summary.density = fpta.reduce_mixture(summary.density, K_reduced)\n",
    "\n",
    "# the step-2 red-noise prior, as a GP on the stand-in pulsar\n",
    "irn = ds.makecommongp_fourier([summary], ds.powerlaw, NRN, T, fourierbasis=fpta.summarybasis, name='red_noise')\n",
    "\n",
    "# note the fpta.makecorrection\n",
    "# this now creates that correction term q / N where q is calculated from the `summary.density`\n",
    "# (mixture here)\n",
    "pslC = ds.PulsarLikelihood([summary.residuals, fpta.makenoise_summary(summary), fpta.makecorrection(summary)])\n",
    "likeC = ds.ArrayLikelihood([pslC], commongp=irn, decenter=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "clogL = jax.jit(likeC.clogL)\n",
    "cname = f'{psr.name}_red_noise_coefficients({2*NRN})'\n",
    "likeC.clogL.params\n",
    "\n",
    "# draw some parameters to test speed\n",
    "rng = np.random.default_rng(0)\n",
    "p = {par: rng.uniform(*ds.prior.getprior_uniform(par, priordict)) for par in rn_pars}\n",
    "p[cname] = jnp.asarray(rng.standard_normal(2 * NRN))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "ba3b7c6d",
   "metadata": {},

    "# check that the reduced GMM representation is ok.\n",
    "# use ??fpta.mixture_kl to understand what's going on.\n",

   ]
  },
  {

    "%%timeit\n",
    "jax.block_until_ready(clogL(p))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "8a79fa29",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "With decentering, the coefficient parameter is the whitened $\\boldsymbol\\xi$, and `clogL` returns the log-density\n",
    "together with the physical coefficients $\\mathbf a(\\boldsymbol\\xi,\\boldsymbol\\eta)$. The log-density already includes the\n",
    "coefficient prior and the Jacobian, so $\\boldsymbol\\xi$ gets a flat prior (the standard-normal draw below is undone by the\n",
    "$+\\tfrac12\\boldsymbol\\xi^\\top\\boldsymbol\\xi$)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "1e00b294",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-07T16:25:35.798505Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-07T16:25:35.798436Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-07T16:28:45.225998Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-07T16:28:45.225695Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "122 s\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "def modelC():\n",
    "    params = {par: numpyro.sample(par, dist.Uniform(*ds.prior.getprior_uniform(par, priordict))) for par in rn_pars}\n",
    "    xi = numpyro.sample('xi', dist.ImproperUniform(dist.constraints.real, (), event_shape=(2*NRN,)))\n",
    "\n",
    "    logp, c = clogL({**params, cname: xi})\n",
    "    numpyro.deterministic('a', c[0])\n",
    "    numpyro.factor('logL', logp) # undo the prior here because it is applied correctly in Discovery under the hood.\n",
    "\n",
    "mcmc = infer.MCMC(infer.NUTS(modelC, max_tree_depth=10), num_warmup=1000, num_samples=4000)\n",
    "t = time.time()\n",
    "mcmc.run(jax.random.key(1))\n",
    "print(f'{time.time() - t:.0f} s')\n",
    "chainC = {par: np.asarray(v) for par, v in mcmc.get_samples().items() if par in rn_pars}"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9cae7d14",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Comparison"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 12,
   "id": "eb0a3501",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-07T16:28:45.227182Z",

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "800eb5d9",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The time domain (A) gives only an upper limit on achromatic red noise ($\\log_{10}A \\lesssim -12.7$ at 95%), while\n",
    "the Gaussian summary (B) reports a confident detection at $\\log_{10}A\\approx-13.0\\pm0.25$. With single-frequency data the\n",
    "excess power can be DM or red noise, and the time-domain posterior keeps both options. The step-1 conditionals know\n",
    "this -- samples with loud DM leave little power in the red-noise coefficients -- but averaging them into one Gaussian\n",
    "loses it. The GMM of those same conditionals (C) recovers the time-domain posterior."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c936e02b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Aside: the GMM marginalized analytically\n",
    "\n",
    "Each mixture component's integral over $\\mathbf a$ against the prior swap is a Gaussian integral, so the GMM can\n",
    "also be marginalized analytically (draft Eq. 21): the likelihood is a log-sum-exp over the components' marginalized likelihoods.\n",
    "This factorizes over pulsars only when the prior does not correlate them, so `mixture_logL` takes the red-noise prior\n",
    "as a common GP (SPNA, IRN, CURN; not HD). It is the same model as C with the coefficients integrated out; each call\n",
    "costs one $2N_\\mathrm{RN}\\times2N_\\mathrm{RN}$ Cholesky factorization per component.\n",
    "\n",
    "Both step-2 likelihoods -- the Gaussian summary's `logL` (B) and the GMM's `mixture_logL` -- are normalized the same\n",
    "way: they are $\\log p(\\delta t\\mid\\boldsymbol\\eta) - \\log p(\\delta t\\mid\\boldsymbol\\eta_0)$, the step-2 marginalized\n",
    "likelihood relative to its value at step 1's reference spectrum. So they can be compared directly, here as the Gaussian-summary and\n",
    "GMM-summary answers to \"how likely is this red-noise spectrum?\":"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 13,
   "id": "26550bb0",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-07T16:28:45.447118Z",

     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-07T16:28:45.657680Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-07T16:28:45.657406Z"
    }
   },

     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",

      "log10_A =  -15.0:  Gaussian summary   120.560   GMM summary   129.456\n",
      "log10_A =  -13.0:  Gaussian summary   132.286   GMM summary   131.779\n",
      "log10_A =  -12.5:  Gaussian summary   121.634   GMM summary   121.572\n",
      "17 ms per call at K = 512\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "logL_gmm = jax.jit(fpta.mixture_logL([summary], irn, K=K))\n",
    "logL_gauss = jax.jit(pslB.logL)\n",
    "\n",
    "for A in [-17.0, -15.0, -13.0, -12.5]:\n",
    "    p = {rn_pars[0]: A, rn_pars[1]: 3.0}\n",
    "    print(f'log10_A = {A:6.1f}:  Gaussian summary {float(logL_gauss(p)):9.3f}   GMM summary {float(logL_gmm(p)):9.3f}')\n",
    "\n",
    "t = time.time(); jax.block_until_ready(logL_gmm(p)); print(f'{(time.time() - t) * 1e3:.0f} ms per call at K = {K}')"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9080e49b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Where the red noise is loud ($\\log_{10}A = -13, -12.5$) the two summaries agree to within about half a unit. Where\n",
    "it is quiet they differ by about 9: as $\\boldsymbol\\varphi(\\boldsymbol\\eta)\\to 0$ this relative marginalized likelihood becomes\n",
    "$\\log q(\\mathbf a = 0) - \\log\\mathcal N(0\\mid 0,\\boldsymbol\\varphi_0)$, i.e. how much density the summary puts on\n",
    "\"no achromatic red noise at all\". The GMM puts much more there -- its components with loud DM leave the red-noise\n",
    "coefficients near zero -- so it does not penalize quiet red noise the way the single Gaussian does. The Gaussian\n",
    "summary favours $\\log_{10}A\\approx-13$ over quiet red noise by about 12 units (a detection), the GMM by about 2: the\n",
    "same difference seen in the posteriors above.\n",
    "\n",
    "The time domain has no column here: its likelihood at fixed red-noise $\\boldsymbol\\eta$ still depends on the DM\n",
    "hyperparameters, and integrating those out is exactly what the two-step method approximates. The time-domain\n",
    "comparison is the posterior comparison above. (With fixed noise in step 1, `summary.logL0` holds\n",
    "$\\log p(\\delta t\\mid\\boldsymbol\\eta_0)$ and these numbers become absolute time-domain marginalized likelihoods; with DM sampled in\n",
    "step 1, as here, that step-1 marginalized likelihood is not computed and `logL0` is 0.)"
   ]
  },
